dossier.public_summary: TESS shows occasional dips around 13.4 days but the depth vanishes in sector 86 and jumps by over 150% between sectors, with individual transits including a negative dip. This level of change refutes a planet on the target. The flat-bottom shape cannot be trusted in the face of such variability and the centroid cannot confirm the signal is on target, so the signal is best explained as noise, systematics or stellar variability, not a planet.

reasons.why: Depth changes by a factor of 152.9 between sectors, with chi2 90.09 dof 2, far beyond any planet variation.
A single source QLP shows depths 14956, 15237 and -102 ppm in sectors 59, 73, 86, proving the variation is astrophysical not calibration.
Individual transit depths are inconsistent with a 5.6 sigma outlier at -631 ppm and a 5.4 sigma outlier at 20392 ppm; one negative detection shows dip is not consistently on eclipse.
Difference imaging has no sector with a clear difference image, so cannot place dip on target; combined with extreme sector instability this leaves a false-alarm/variability explanation as best.
A star within one TESS pixel can produce this depth, and high RUWE 4.348 plus variability flag on a 0.4468 Rsun dwarf favours spot/systematic over planet.
